findings.summary: The BeanFactory vs ApplicationContext table is stated as a table with a vague 'Use' row, and the 'Startup and Scanning' flow steps are listed as bare fragments with no labels connecting them.
findings.evidence: "Read config / annotations / Java config / BeanDefinitions / built / Instantiate / Inject / dependencies / Init callbacks"
findings.fix: Present the startup as a labelled flow: Read config -> Build BeanDefinitions -> Instantiate -> Inject -> Init callbacks.

findings.summary: Bullet packs two ideas: the benefits of constructor injection are listed in one run-on line.
findings.evidence: "Constructor: immutable, required, testable with plain new, never half-built"
findings.fix: Split into a short comparison table (Constructor vs Field) with one benefit per row.

findings.summary: The ObjectProvider example never shows Job declared as a prototype, so it does not show why getObject() returns a fresh instance each call.
findings.evidence: private final ObjectProvider<Job> jobs; ... jobs.getObject().go(); — 'getObject() returns a fresh prototype each call'
findings.fix: Add a Job class annotated @Component @Scope("prototype") to the snippet.

findings.summary: Bullet holds two ideas: the singleton scope definition and the thread-safety rule.
findings.evidence: "Singleton is one per container, not per JVM" / "Shared by all threads, so keep it stateless" plus table note "stateless or thread-safe" versus "keep it stateless"
findings.fix: State one consistent rule (stateless, or thread-safe if it holds state) and keep the per-container point on its own line.

findings.summary: Code is shown after the bullets but the 'Do not call another bean method to wire' rule sits in a bullet that gives no reason, and the tension with 'repeated bean-method calls return the same singleton' is unexplained.
findings.evidence: "Class is CGLIB-proxied: repeated bean-method calls return the same singleton" vs "Do not call another bean method to wire"
findings.fix: Add one line: calls are safe in full mode but prefer method parameters, which also work in lite mode.

findings.summary: The @ConfigurationProperties record example is not registered as a bean, so binding would not happen if a learner copied it.
findings.fix: Add a note and annotation: register it with @ConfigurationPropertiesScan or @EnableConfigurationProperties(AppProps.class), or annotate it with @Component.

findings.summary: A code block is shown with a one-line caption that does not state the idea (when to use @Value versus @ConfigurationProperties).
findings.fix: Replace with two bullets: @Value for a single value with a default; @ConfigurationProperties for grouped, type-safe settings.

findings.summary: The cheat sheet says a prototype bean is created 'per request', which readers will confuse with the web request scope.
findings.evidence: prototype | New per request | No destroy call
findings.fix: Change to 'New instance per injection or getBean/ObjectProvider lookup', matching the wording on page 3.

findings.summary: The cheat sheet says a prototype bean is 'New per request', which a learner will read as per HTTP request, not per injection or lookup.
findings.evidence: prototype | New per request | No destroy call
findings.fix: Change to 'New per injection or lookup' so it is not confused with request scope, which the next row covers.

findings.summary: Terms are used inconsistently for prototype scope: 'New per request' on the cheat sheet conflicts with the 'request' web scope and with page 3's 'new per injection or lookup'.
findings.evidence: "prototype | New per request | No destroy call"
findings.fix: Change to 'New per injection or lookup' to match page 3.
